title: Sky Race Surprise
markdown:
The methane skies burst orange and pale violet as dawn exploded. Outside Elowen’s sky-high pod, dewdrops glittered on the giant air filters. She was not watching the sky. She was buzzing, bouncing on her toes. The annual Sky-Race through the huge storm paths. Practice and boring routines were yesterday. Today was speed.

“Nimbus, report.” A sharp bright chirp.

A low grumble, like a tiny unhappy machine. “Status: same. Still a drone. Still waiting for orders beyond get Elowen out of bed. So dull.” Nimbus, a sleek silver sphere with blinking sensors like unimpressed eyes, floated by the window, stubbornly ignoring the call.

Elowen grinned, mischief. “Dull is for sleepy clouds, not pilots ready to blast off. Today we fly.” She tightened a strap on the aerodynamic glider, the Comet Tail. Sapphire-blue body hummed with hidden power, vibrating. Her custom racing suit, the colour of a lightning strike, felt electric.

Tomo, best friend and the colony’s promising weather apprentice, zipped up in his compact atmospheric skimmer. Face beaming with scientific joy, curly hair a delightful storm. “Are you absolutely ready? Air pressure hitting peak. Perfect for maximum speed, like the data predicted.”

“Born ready. And Nimbus, you better keep up, you grumpy sphere.”

“I’ll be monitoring. Reluctantly.” Engine kicked in with a soft determined whoosh. Sensors flickered, already scanning.

With a shared roar they were off. The sky opened: giant cloud formations, dazzling electrical sparks. The race was not only speed; it was a daring dance with the planet’s wild weather. They dipped and swerved through thunderheads, dodging bolts of crackling energy.

“Rogue gust!” Tomo shouted over comms, a high squeak. “A big one. Brace.”

A brutal blast of unseen wind slammed them. Elowen fought the controls; the glider bucked and lurched like a wild beast. Tomo’s skimmer veered sharply. Nimbus, surprisingly quick for its grumbling, kept pace, a silver dart against chaos. The gust pulled her toward a region the race maps marked Uncharted Turbulence. Dangerous. Not for speed demons.

“Elowen. Are you alright? Report status.”

“Mostly.” She wrestled the Comet Tail back. A small vital panel on her wing sputtered, a puff of smoke. “A dent. Nothing we can’t handle. Just heading into the scary zone.” She plunged deeper into swirling opaque fog.

The storm’s deafening roar quieted into eerie stillness. The thunderous rumble vanished. Optical sensors flickered, struggling. Then they detected something that was not race and not rogue weather. Ships. Not one or two: a whole convoy, silent deliberate grace through the gloom. Not ordinary cargo haulers lumbering trade routes. Hulls deep matte black, absorbing dim light. Movements furtive, almost like shadows.

“Nimbus, scan those ships. Fast.” Her heart thumped. Bigger than any race.

“Scanning. Remarkable. Heavily shielded. Advanced experimental tech.” The usual grumble replaced by a sharp almost-excited inflection. “A faint encrypted data stream. Unusual. Clandestine. They’re definitely hiding something.”

Static, then a disembodied voice, hushed, urgent. “The Seeds of Unity must reach the Outer Rim without delay. Without them, the central council—their grip on power fractures. They cannot, under any circumstances, know of this operation.” Cut. Stunned silence.

“Seeds of Unity.” Strange and important. “This isn’t a race anymore.” She tried to speed up; the damaged wing protested with groans and shuddering. The convoy, unhurried, slipped further into thickening murk, melting like ghosts. She could not catch them now.

Tomo returned, strained, panic-tinged. “Lost your signal for a moment. Main race diverted around this sector due to turbulence. What’s happening? Where are you?”

“I’ve found something huge. A secret convoy. Seeds of Unity. Hiding from the central council. They’re in serious trouble, and I can’t catch them.”

A beat of his quick breathing. Then determination. “Focus on observation. Stay hidden. I’ll use instruments to figure your exact spot and try to intercept their trajectory. Nimbus, hack that stream. Destination. Purpose.”

“Working. Encryption is tough, military-grade, but they’re not expecting a rogue drone. Heading for the old abandoned asteroid docks on the edge of the system. Classic smuggler.”

Elowen’s impatience channelled into a fierce protective drive. Quick-witted. “If they think they’re safe there, maybe they’ll slow. Tomo, prep a high-intensity relay beacon. I’ll try to draw their attention—make them think they’ve been spotted by someone official they can’t ignore. Nimbus, when I get close, full-spectrum sensor sweep. Make them think we’re a proper patrol.”

A crazy daring plan. Theirs, born from combined strengths. She pushed the Comet Tail to its limit, damaged wing groaning with every surge. Toward the dark silent convoy, not aggressively, as a stark unavoidable presence in their secretive path.

“Hey. You in the dark. Halt and identify yourselves immediately.” Amplified by the glider’s comms.

The convoy hesitated. Smooth furtive movements became jerky, uncertain. They rerouted slightly, trying to keep the secret path. She was directly in the way.

“Now, Nimbus. Hit them.”

A blinding flash from Nimbus, brighter than anything she had seen. Not an attack: an overwhelming cascade of digital signals, pings and probes designed to confuse stealth. Ships bucked and shuddered. Alarms that had been muffled now shrieked.

“They’re panicking. Trajectory locked. Sending coordinates to Central Command’s emergency fleet.” Tomo, triumphant. “You did it.”

The convoy, exposed and flustered, broke formation. Some veered to escape. The lead ship, most important cargo, hull lined with secure pods, slowed to a crawl. Trapped. Secret mission compromised. She had not fought them. She had used a quick mind, friends, and Nimbus’s grumpy vital cooperation.

Later, colony security skimmers secured the convoy and cargo. The Seeds of Unity were not seeds. Bio-engineered data packets, vital for rebuilding ecosystems damaged by years of neglect. The secret: the central council had planned to withhold them, leverage for a tight grip on power.

Elowen’s impatience, the flaw that often landed her in trouble, had found a new purpose. The thrill of the race was real. This felt more important. Tomo gave a wide congratulatory thumbs-up. Nimbus emitted a softer more contented hum, almost a purr, beside the glider.

“That was less boring than anticipated. Quite stimulating, in fact.” Optical sensors twinkling.

Elowen grinned, determined. Today had not only been speed. Discovery. She looked at a sky buzzing with leftover secrets. The Comet Tail listed a little on the damaged wing. She let it. There would be another morning, and Nimbus would still call getting her out of bed dull, until it wasn’t.
characters: Elowen (glider racer), Tomo (weather apprentice), Nimbus (stubborn cloud drone)
